author: DaiqingChen
body:
Currently, only the gene products of protein complexes are annotated to this term.

Add annotations for **all** gene products under this term:
[260408_non-collagenous component of interstitial matrix annotation QC.xlsx](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26578803/260408_non-collagenous.component.of.interstitial.matrix.annotation.QC.xlsx)

**Google spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/17wza0mcufyFVlyvl3_iCL8IWIHTfPxn818nYFxHSh54/edit?gid=0#gid=0**

**About the file:** 
This list contains 163 non-collagenous genes that is active or located in the non-collagenous part of interstitial matrix. Among these 163 genes, 41 genes is active in the interstitial matrix, 122 is located in the interstitial matrix. The qualifier column is stating the status of how the relationship should be add. 
The last column is a checker of the location of protein, there are 141 genes only exist in interstitial matrix (IM), 22 genes exist both in the basement membrane and interstitial matrix (BM & IM). The qualifier column is stating the relationship of gene and the Non-collagenous component of interstitial matrix(GO:0140149) term.

All genes have evidence located in the ECM, either from MatrisomDB PMID: 36399478, or individual publication source.

**Next step:**
Will run another QC of all annotations of interstitial matrix genes after adding all non-collagenous component of interstitial matrix.

author: pgaudet
body:
Regarding CRISPLD1: 

We had talked about asking InterPro to add a mapping; however the corresponding InterPro entries mention several subcellular locations,  see https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/InterPro/IPR014044/ and https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/InterPro/IPR051957/. 


So, this approach doesn't works. It seems we don't have enough data to annotate this one. 

I looked for papers describing CRISPLD1 as an ECM protein, suggested by AI, and found these: 

https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26794603/
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7060963/

but I cannot find the data there. DO you have any evidence we can use ?

author: Matrisome
body:
@pgaudet I think the paper by Wilson (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26794603/) provides good experimental evidence that CRISPLD1 is in the interstitial ECM. Table 2 lists it as a protein detected by proteomics in cartilage explants, and cartilage is ~95% ECM and 5% cells! 
Together with the fact that we have predicted, based on sequence analysis, that CRISPLD1 is part of the matrisome ( PMC3322572), I think there is sufficient evidence to list this gene product under GO:0140149.

author: pgaudet
body:
